claims.statement: The advance-payment fee schedule is stored as a JSON array under settings.key='advance_payment_fee_schedules'; per-entry CRUD parses the JSON, mutates the slice, and writes the row back inside SELECT … FOR UPDATE so concurrent edits cannot lose a tier.

FeeScheduleEntry.Validate enforces at least one tier, first tier MinAmount=0, strictly increasing tiers, percentages in [0,100], MinFeeVND >= 0 (0 disables the floor for a fully free advance), and YYYY-MM-DD effective_date.

ResolveFee picks the highest-MinAmount tier whose MinAmount <= amount and returns max(amount * percentage / 100, MinFeeVND); ActiveFeeScheduleAt returns the entry with the latest EffectiveDate <= at so ad-hoc preview and disbursement-time fee calculation always agree.

project_employees.advance_request_enabled (migration 105, TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 1) is a per-employee kill switch for new advance requests (regular and self-check-in flows); 0 blocks new requests only and leaves existing pending/approved requests untouched.

flexpay_salary_notifications (migration 100) is the durable delivery record for salary notifications, with a UNIQUE (asset_id, project_id, employee_id, template_id) key for safe import retry and a (status, lease_expires_at) index for the recovery sweeper.

FlexPay salary notifications use a lease-based claim model (Claim, ReleaseForRetry, MarkSent/Failed/Suppressed, ListRecoverable); the asynq worker flexpay_salary_notification_worker.go consumes the queue and a recovery sweeper re-claims stale leases.

FlexPay advances are paid out of the wallet: the disbursement service books a wallet_payment, the disbursement_execute_worker calls the active provider (OnePay prod, 9Pay sandbox), and the IPN handler drives the wallet state machine through ipn_completed / ipn_failed / ipn_reversed triggers.
flex_pay_settlement_service.go runs inside a transaction so advance_payment_request settlement, ledger entries, and the salary batch row commit atomically.
